summary: Coimbra is a dense Euro where each round you draft dice that double as currency, action-strength, and a track-advancement resource, forcing constant trade-offs about what to give up. It rewards building engines across several interlocking tracks (ships, coins, monastery favors) that all pay off at game end.
praised: tight interlocking economy with real trade-offs
criticised: steep rules overhead and analysis paralysis
bidding/dice-drafting can feel fiddly to teach
some randomness in dice rolls frustrates planners
can run long for a mid-weight game

interaction.kind: drafting from shared pools with light board conflict
interaction.detail: Each round players draft dice and buy cards from common shared displays, so taking one denies it to opponents, and ships move along a shared discovery board where positioning matters. Most building, production, and scoring still happen on each player's own personal tableau.

scoring.how_you_win: Play out exactly four rounds drafting and spending dice on tracks, voyages, and characters, then tally influence-track position bonuses, voyage rewards, diplomas, pilgrim progress, and leftover resources; whoever has the most total VP wins (ties go to earlier turn order).
